newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt could be tiger but lacks bite - U.S.economist.
newsitem.headline: Egypt could be tiger but lacks bite - U.S.economist.

text.p: Egypt could be one of the next generation of rapidly industrialising countries built on cheap manufacturing but for the moment its economic policy remains too "soft", a leading U.S. economist said on Monday.

Anne Krueger, professor of economics at Stanford University and an expert on trade and development, said in a lecture that the world needed new countries to replace the East Asian exporters such as Korea and Taiwan.

"If I look at Egypt, the low wages, Egypt's very favourable geographic position, the very vibrant entrepreneurial community and a number of other advantages it does seem to me that Egypt might be a candidate," she told the prestigious Egyptian Centre for Economic Studies in Cairo.
She said she was talking of countries that have concentrated on labour-intensive and unskilled-labour manufacturing aimed at export to achieve double-digit growth for 10 to 20 years.
But the key to success, she added, was "single-minded purpose and commitment" so that all members of society become convinced that this is the way to go.

"Then the focus on getting the improved economic performance becomes so great that many of the distractions of economic policy that are normally what make it go softer at the sides disappear," she said.
"It would be my impression that in Egypt reforms have come a long way but that Egyptian policy in my sense is still soft.

"There's still lots and lots of concern that there are things that are done for good sufficient reason but they may at the margin detract from getting the singleminded reorientation of policy geared towards rapid economic development," she added.
The Egyptian government's economic liberalisation programme has brought GDP growth up to a consistent five percent but its attempts to stimulate exports have made almost no headway.
Krueger did not go into details of how the Egyptian government might improve its policies.
